findings.title: Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks
findings.body: When an override applies, this branch returns true before checking `busy`. A user with a 10:00–11:00 override and an existing 10:00–10:30 booking or calendar event will therefore have the occupied 10:00 slot advertised as available. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their overrides into this function. Overrides should replace working hours, not bypass busy-time checks.

findings.title: Require the entire slot to fit inside the override
findings.body: These checks reject only completely disjoint intervals, so partial overlap is treated as availability. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 candidate generated by a rotating host, even though the fixed host is unavailable for the first half-hour. Check that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

findings.title: Check the actual slot end against working hours
findings.body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again, so the event duration is ignored. With a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 UTC, a rotating host's override can generate a 60-minute 09:30–10:30 candidate that passes this check as if it ended at 09:30. This still offers round-robin events extending beyond the fixed host's availability.

findings.title: Treat working-hour windows as alternatives
findings.body: The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hour window excludes it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same weekday, morning slots are rejected by the afternoon window and afternoon slots by the morning window, leaving no availability. A slot should be accepted when it fits one applicable window, not required to fit every window.

findings.title: Do not reject valid slots against another override window
findings.body: A date can contain multiple override intervals, but this search rejects a slot whenever it is disjoint from any interval on that date. With 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 UTC overrides, the valid 10:00 slot is rejected by the second interval and the valid 14:00 slot by the first. Consequently, split date overrides lose all their slots, including on personal events.

findings.title: Split timezone-converted overrides across attendee dates
findings.body: Keeping only the converted hour and minute discards date rollover. A 10:00–12:00 UTC override viewed in Pacific/Tongatapu (UTC+13) becomes 23:00–01:00, represented here as startTime 1380 and endTime 60. `buildSlots` skips that range because its start exceeds its end, so the availability disappears instead of being split across two attendee dates.

findings.title: Avoid applying DST compensation twice to overrides
findings.body: These offsets use the override date, but `buildSlots` subsequently applies `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` based on today's offsets. If New York is currently UTC−5 and a future 10:00–11:00 override occurs while it is UTC−4, a UTC attendee's slot is correctly converted to 14:00 here, then shifted back to 13:00 by `buildSlots` and rejected by the availability check. Already date-adjusted overrides must not receive that second DST correction.
